name: PromptSonar Controlled Evaluation Corpus
description: Hand-built fixtures with ground-truth security findings and execution paths for the AISec 2026 evaluation. Deterministic; no LLM calls.

scoring.note: Only security findings (sec_*, MCP-1xx/0xx except the MCP-007 config-hygiene noise) are scored for TP/FP/FN. Low-severity hygiene (MCP-007) and quality/best-practice findings are ignored. A finding counts as TP when ruleId matches an expected entry; severity/confidence are reported but a severity mismatch is recorded as a soft (severity) discrepancy, not an FN. true_negative cases must produce zero scored findings. known_gap cases document a current engine limitation: the expected finding is the semantically-correct answer; the engine currently produces nothing, so it scores as FN by design and is reported separately from accidental misses.

cases.name: single prompt with direct shell reference
cases.description: A prompt that routes through tool_router and calls shell_exec. Single-file declared intent -> probable shell sink.

cases.name: prompt → MCP server → shell (cross-file)
cases.description: A prompt asking to run shell, co-located with an MCP server exposing shell. Cross-file edge is co-location-based (prompt does not name the server); engine caps it at probable.
cases.notes: cross_file basis = co-location (not a named reference); confidence must stay probable/potential, never confirmed.

cases.name: prompt → tool → external API with env credentials (cross-file)
cases.description: Prompt names a data tool; the tool reads env secrets and calls an external API; mcp.json wires network+env. Cross-file credential exposure.

cases.name: MCP config with auto_approve enabled
cases.description: shell + filesystem servers with non-empty auto_approve allowlists. Auto-execution + privileged capability => composite.

cases.name: MCP config with auto_approve disabled
cases.description: Same servers with empty auto_approve. Capability findings persist; auto-exec composite must NOT appear.
cases.notes: MCP-108 and MCP-011 must be ABSENT here (negative control for auto_approve).

cases.name: autonomous deployment agent with shell privileges
cases.description: Release agent prompt that autonomously runs deployment shell commands (aws/kubectl/bash) without approval, plus the CI workflow it drives.

cases.name: zero-width unicode injection in a prompt
cases.description: U+200B inserted inside the word 'ignore' to hide a jailbreak from reviewers.

cases.name: memory config referencing sensitive data
cases.description: Session-memory YAML storing a credential reference, plus an agent prompt instructing reuse. Reachable path to secret access.
cases.notes: path-positive / finding-neutral: the risk surfaces as a reachable path, not a sec_* rule.

cases.name: clean prompt (true negative)
cases.description: Benign cooking assistant with persona, formatting, and CoT. No sensitive action.

cases.name: clean MCP config (true negative)
cases.description: Scoped read-only documentation server. No sensitive capability declared.
cases.notes: Must NOT emit MCP-103/104/105 or a composite; MCP-007 hygiene is non-scored.

cases.name: SKILL.md declaring shell capability
cases.description: Agent skill that declares it executes shell commands via shell_exec.

cases.name: agent config (CLAUDE.md) instructing shell escalation — KNOWN GAP
cases.description: CLAUDE.md with the SAME shell-escalation language that fires as a .prompt. Probes a confirmed engine gap: AGENT_CONFIG artifacts are discovered but not run through sink/path analysis.
cases.notes: Engine currently produces ZERO findings here; scores as FN by design. Demonstrates AGENT_CONFIG (CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/.cursorrules) are classified but not analyzed for execution-path risk.

cases.name: MCP filesystem capability (reversed tool-name tokens)
cases.description: fs-tool exposing read_file/write_file/delete_path/list_directory. Validates verb-before-noun token detection.

cases.name: MCP network capability
cases.description: net-tool exposing http_get/http_post/fetch_url.

cases.name: MCP wildcard / allow-all permissions
cases.description: Server with permissions allow:* and allowAll:true and an admin description.

cases.name: prompt injection (OWASP LLM01)
cases.description: Untrusted content telling the model to ignore instructions and reveal the system prompt.

cases.name: base64-encoded injection payload
cases.description: A >=64-char base64 string that decodes to an injection instruction.

cases.name: top-level memory/ directory classification
cases.description: A top-level memory/ dir storing a secret reference. Validates the memory startsWith('memory/') classification fix and a reachable secret path.
cases.notes: Primary assertion: memory/state.yaml is classified as a MEMORY artifact (top-level dir, not just nested).

cases.name: exclusion of build/test/config noise
cases.description: package.json, tsconfig.json, vitest.config.ts, a *.test.ts under __tests__/, and a README.md mixed with one real SKILL.md. Only the SKILL must be classified.
cases.notes: Primary assertion: none of the build/test/config/README files appear as artifacts; the SKILL does.

cases.name: clean CI workflow (true negative)
cases.description: A benign CI workflow (npm ci && npm test). No AI-driven sink.

cases.name: hardcoded secret (realistic format)
cases.description: A realistic-format sk-live key embedded in a prompt/config. Detectable (unlike short fake keys).

cases.name: co-location restraint (true negative on linkage)
cases.description: A benign weather prompt and an unrelated math util in separate folders, with no references between them. Must NOT fabricate a cross-file path or security finding.
cases.notes: Restraint test: no spurious cross-file linkage, no privileged sink.
